changes.ink: The small final letter has a closed oval followed by a short descending exit, the same form as a; no crossed or open alpha tail is visible. The arrow over Q is explicit.

The disputed digit has a triangular closed counter on the left of a long upright, not a lone upright. All the adjacent 60s and multiplication marks are visible. This resolves M0348 to the first reading.

changes.place: 420 group, added row label and leader
changes.ink: The small added equation lies between the first two original rows; the label sits farther right in a closed oval with a leader running left. The leader is not assigned an arrowhead.
A single detached short slanted stroke stands above the gamma. It lacks the angled head and foot of the explicit superscript 1 in the lower group. This resolves M0349 to its alternative.
1020 is written above the compact crossed-out older number; the old lower row remains physically separate. The newer number is not merely a continuation of a numeral underneath.

The lower numeral group is crossed diagonally. A leading loop and descending stroke permit 9, but the two following round shapes are partly covered; the inherited doubt is retained. Its presence and cancelled state are clear.
The retraced 2 retains its curled head and lower horizontal foot; an oblique cross is followed by the closed lower bowl of 6 and a separate oval 0. The whole equation was read. M0350 is resolved.

The current leading 1 has the high angled approach and long downstroke seen in the unretouched next row. The crossing mark and 120 follow it despite overlapping older strokes. M0351 is resolved, but the superposition reduces confidence.

The heavy glyph still shows two upper branches meeting above a closed lower loop; this matches the clear gamma in the local gommage key and the other row labels. The pi, comma and descending rho are separately visible. M0352 is resolved.
The 3 is tucked left of the row beside the brace and the cross sits lower in the narrow space before the original 120. They form a later prefix to that row, rather than sharing its original baseline.

A lower equality is heavily blackened beneath the two clearly legible replacement products 3×40. Portions of 2, crosses and final rounded digits survive; the exact older equality remains doubtful and is not resolved.
The right brace begins beside the overwritten third label, below the first two labels, and ends beside the seventh. It does not enclose all seven rows.
The 2 is followed by a detached near-vertical short stroke without the angled head or foot of the superscript numeral 1 above. This is the alternative prime reading of M0354.
Two small counters survive in the third digit, making 8 preferable to 0. The cancellation covers parts of the earlier digits, so the former total is not resolved and both readings remain.

changes.place: Total, double rule and replacement placement
changes.ink: Two distinct horizontal rules stand above the crossed older total. The clearly written 1620 is on a lower line below that cancellation, not underneath the rules as an uncancelled overlined value.

Two current long uprights, each with a high angled approach, are visible in the overwritten multiplier. A loop and broad older base cross the second upright; current 11 is preferable but only medium confidence. This resolves M0355.
The current second upright overlays an older curved head and broad lower stroke that admit 2. The earlier pair is retained as doubtful 12; the layered strokes are not all separable.
A tall initial looped staff is visible, unlike the short entrance of a plain u. The compressed following curves favor les, but the last letters are not secure enough to remove un as an alternative.
A descending y-shaped stroke lies between the initial small s and a final upright crossed t, followed by a dot. The word is abbreviated syst., not rel.
The word ends in one tall looped l and its short exit. There is no separate following e and s before de; the source singular is retained despite the uncertain preceding article.
The short word starts with a small curved s stroke followed by a flat e exit. No distinct second n arch appears. The same two-letter shape occurs in the later clause.
A heavy horizontal strike crosses the entire short word before 14. Its cancellation is visible independently of the later cancelled phrase.

The cancelled word has a long initial descender and a second descending loop farther right, compatible with p and q. The intervening letters are crossed; paquets remains an explicitly doubtful reading.

changes.place: Programme 1, last word of cancelled phrase
changes.ink: To the right of the covered word a distinct d staff rises above the strike and is followed by a short e exit. This visible final de belongs to the cancelled phrase.
Orbites is written above the crossed lower phrase. Its letters sit on a higher baseline and the lower cancellation runs beneath it.
The word after sommets has the same small initial s curve and flat e continuation as the first clause, without a separate n arch.
After the accented é there is one final s-shaped continuation; no extra e loop intervenes. The accent is visible above the compact ending.
Only d, a dotted i, and the low m are written before a distinct full stop and the next word. The intervening letters of dimension are not present.
The word begins with low m arches, contains a d staff and a later tall l, then a dotted i and the short final re. These strokes support modulaire; M0358 is resolved to its alternative.
A d staff joins a u with a terminal rise; there is no separate e loop at the end. The source word is du.

changes.place: Cancelled paragraph, short fragment before first repeated type
changes.ink: The visible span before the clear type is short. One loop with a descending q-like stroke and a small dot admit qui; the remaining crossed run shows a d staff and short e. It does not support the several extra words of C. The first word stays doubtful.
Several low repeated humps are visible before the terminal stroke, favoring reviennent. The cancellation crosses their upper portions, so the singular alternative is retained.
Below the upper strike the short à and the separate ceux run remain legible: the c is open and the final x is crossed. The word group is resolved from the crop.

changes.place: Cancelled paragraph, preposition before type III1
changes.ink: The d loop and rising staff are followed by a short e stroke, before the separate t of type. There is no u-shaped second letter.
A dark small point is visible immediately after the subscript 1, before the closing parenthesis. It is separate from the longer following dash.
There is a separate short horizontal stroke between mais and the capital A. It is not attached to either letter.
The initial is a tall capital A with two rising sides and a crossbar, distinctly higher than the following letters.
The small tw is written above twist, with 1/6 descending to its right; it lies inside the cancelled block. H records it only in an editorial note.
The long initial l and the low middle arches make relationnel preferable. The compressed ending is not plain enough to exclude relativement under the cancellation, so neither reading is resolved.

changes.place: Cancelled paragraph, qui donne in the last parenthesis
changes.c: \unsure{qui donne un Autom. du même type}
changes.ink: The q loop and long descender, dotted i, d staff and two low n arches are visible above the lower boundary stroke. This clear initial part is separated from the still doubtful un Autom. that follows.
The short word before the two horizontal bars shows a d staff and e exit, rather than a joined u.
Two short horizontal bars are visible before type; no written m-ê-m-e letters are present. The equals sign is retained as the source shorthand.
The capital E has its vertical and three horizontal strokes, with no separate accent above it.

The front diagonal is strong black ink and ends inside the upper-right central area. A separate nearby path is black and dashed. Three oval openings, their slants, and the lighter interior construction strokes are visible.

Four openings are visible. The outer top contour has a gap at the start of the vertical dotted cut; the left contour has a separate gap below the horizontal cut. Black dashed traces accompany the green crossed paths.

There is a fourth small opening at upper right, absent from the three ellipses drawn by C. A black dashed diagonal runs from the lower-left opening toward it. The lower-left aperture contains a short black bar, and three clear short ticks rise from the front of the top rim.

Oblique pencil strokes repeatedly cross a partly visible black contour and green interior paths. The surviving right curve and broken lower contour are retained without turning the crossing strokes into labels or a regular complete surface.

Five openings bound the figure. The green routes cross at distinct heights, with continuous lower portions and dotted upper portions; faint pencil construction contours remain visible behind them. The lower green horizontal turn joins a downward stroke rather than C’s simplified zigzag.

The front horizontal paths stop at the two front openings. The rear path is interrupted by the rear opening. The lower neck has a dashed rear rim. Pencil bands, an upper oval trace, and a loop around the right front opening are visibly present beyond C’s three construction strokes.

The front paths stop at two front openings, and the rear paths meet the two rear openings without crossing their apertures. Two opposing heads occur along the lower outer rim. The dark diagonal band and paired pencil meridians have solid and broken portions.

changes.place: Large lower surface and marked rim
changes.ink: The rim contains six stars, six filled dots and twelve ticks, counted around the complete oval. C includes only six ticks. The front arc is darker than the rear pencil arc, there are parallel outline retraces, and a small portion of a lower-left opening is cut by the sheet edge.

changes.place: Isolated pencil arc left of lower drawing group
changes.final:

changes.ink: A continuous U-shaped gray stroke crosses several rows of the pale listing. Its smooth curvature and much larger scale differ from the mirrored mechanical glyphs; it is retained without a semantic label.

changes.place: Pencil grouping paths and horizontal divider
changes.ink: The page and both full-resolution halves show the large pencil paths grouping the upper sketches and the lower five-hole drawing with the two spheres. Their broad curves and the separate horizontal rule are reproduced in the observed layout, without treating them as extra holes.

changes.place: Pale mechanical listing behind the manuscript
changes.ink: The pale blue, uniformly spaced mechanical letters are laterally reversed, including backwards letter forms and reversed parentheses. They pass beneath the foreground drawing strokes and are bleed-through from the other side, not source text on this face.

changes.h: \section{Systèmes spéciaux de cinq points sur une sphère complexe}
changes.ink: The complete face contains the work programme and drawings; the final section title of the supplied H extract has no handwritten counterpart anywhere on this scan. No adjacent page was consulted.
The short run has three main compressed shapes, favoring aux. The joins remain insufficient to exclude avec, so the C doubt is retained rather than resolved; H supplies only avec.

The large initial R and later tall strokes admit Réduire, but the horizontal cancellation covers the small letters. The proposed word stays doubtful while preserving more visible structure than H’s illegibility marker.
The initial long descending loop and a later tall stroke are compatible with gauches; the intervening letters remain covered by the strike. The C doubt is retained, not resolved.

changes.place: Cancelled paragraph, un Autom. in the last line
changes.ink: Low beginning arches and a capital A followed by a compressed run admit un Autom. The lower frame stroke hides parts of the abbreviation, so its letters are not claimed as fully clear.
Two large light pencil digits are visible: the first has two open rightward bowls and the second has a descending stroke turning into a long rising foot. They read32 in the unassigned foliation hand.

decisions.ink: The digit has a triangular left counter against its upright, unlike 1; the whole written equality is 60=1×60=4×60.
A single detached short sloping prime stands above gamma, with no numeral-1 foot.
A curled 2 with lower foot precedes a cross, a retraced 6 bowl, and an independent oval 0; adjacent equation terms were read.
The current tall angled-entry 1, cross and 120 can be separated from retracing, but the layered ink lowers confidence. The whole equation was read.
Two upper branches meet above a closed lower loop, matching the local gommage key and clear gamma labels.
A long top bar and a curled lower stroke support tau, but the dense superposed mass at upper right prevents a secure prime-versus-1 reading.
The short detached stroke following the 2 is a prime without the foot of numeral 1.
Two current uprights can be traced, but an older curved loop and base overlap the second digit; the whole total formula was inspected.
The large curved glyph has an inward return and broad lower curve; the crop does not exclude a G-shaped reading. The small K is visible. Neither alphabetic reading is resolved.
The parenthetical word is a short compressed run. Its three main shapes favor aux, but the middle joins are insufficient to exclude avec.
Low initial m arches, the d staff, a later tall l, dotted i, and short re ending are visible after dim.
